ihs_outlook.outlook_description: The return of major cocoa smuggling underlines the propensity of officials to be easily suborned given sufficient financial inducement.
Access to West African Central Bank reduces foreign exchange shortage risks.
Ethnic and religious differences are likely to become a trigger for politically motivated conflict around the presidential election in October 2025.
A new Mining Code is imminent, although the main changes are likely to revolve around local content.
Score affirmation: There is unlikely to be any significant difference in the efficiency of commercial courts in the 12-month outlook.
Likelihood of sustained high US interest rates and protectionism heightens the risk of depreciation, potentially leading to increased import costs.
Score affirmation: Despite ramping up of oil production, there appears no threat of the state oil company being given a larger share of concessions.
President Ouattara is likely to stand again in October 2025 and will face a moderately strong challenge from a re-emerging opposition.
Inflation could be boosted by currency weakness due to the strength of the US Dollar.
Steady improvements in transport infrastructure are likely to continue, particularly projects to relieve congestion in urban centres.
Junta-led Sahel states have accused Ivorian security forces of fomenting destabilisation, increasing the possibility of cross-border confrontations.
Another substantial increase in the farmgate price for cocoa is likely to reduce strike risks, although lower yields remain a concern.
Score affirmation: Significant changes affecting business operations are unlikely to be introduced before the October 2025 presidential election.
The protest risk is likely to start rising as the presidential election approaches, but gatherings will remain suppressed and relatively small.
Higher domestic inflation and global outlook weakness impacts economic outlook.
With a new Mining Code likely now coming before the election, the emphasis is firmly on forcing companies to comply with local content rules.
Decrease in Sovereign default risk
Score affirmation: State finances are likely to remain stable after being shored up by multilateral support to reinforce steady economic growth.
Engagement with an ongoing IMF support programme renders it unlikely that the country will need to impose ad hoc taxes or penalties to meet spending.
Steady movement towards the West African Monetary Union convergence criteria of a 3% fiscal deficit indicates no requirement for tax increases.
Effective securing of the northern frontier is staving off the threat of jihadist attacks despite the continuing weakness of Sahel neighbours.
GDP per capita is forecast to increase by 10.2%.
